content.text: Document structure confirms this is a securitization Transfer and Servicing Agreement, with no covenants/restrictive-covenant article. My searches across "compete," "competing," "exclusiv," "shall not engage," "field of use," "territor," "similar business," and "restrict" returned only boilerplate (forum language, account-control provisions, and no-contravention reps).

input.quote: petition a court of competent jurisdiction to appoint
input.rationale: This rule is satisfied at the preferred position by absence. The Agreement is a securitization Transfer and Servicing Agreement and contains no non-compete, exclusivity, field-of-use or territorial restriction binding our party (the Issuer, Verizon Owner Trust 2020-A, or the Depositor, Verizon ABS LLC). Targeted searches for "compete", "competing", "shall not engage", "field of use", "territor", "similar business" and "solicit" produced no restrictive-covenant language: the only matches for "compete" are the standard forum phrase "court of competent jurisdiction" (p0335, p0469). The "exclusiv" hits are unrelated — Section 9 concerns notices of exclusive control over the Cap Collateral Account (an account-control mechanic, not a business restriction), and Section 10.6 is a nonexclusive submission to jurisdiction. The "restrict" hits are ordinary no-contravention representations referring to pre-existing contractual restrictions, plus a Successor Servicer carve-out for information subject to third-party transfer or confidentiality restrictions, which limits a disclosure obligation rather than restricting what businesses we may operate. Nothing here constrains the products or services our party may buy, build or market, so no redline is warranted. Note for the file: because the Issuer and Depositor are special-purpose entities whose permitted activities are already narrowly circumscribed by their own organizational documents and the transaction documents, any future addition of a field-of-use or non-compete covenant should be resisted as unnecessary.
